transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-16
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood SA - observing), Dr. Priya Rao (AegisMed), Carlos Mendes, Jenna Park, Theo Alvarez

Summary (auto): scoping dedicated/reserved GPU pool needs, isolation (VPC vs private), burst/fallback behaviour and pilot plan. Customer cares about predictable p99 latency, cost per token/seq, and security attestations.

--- Transcript (imperfect ASR, occasional mis-hearings) ---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everybody, thanks for carving time, I'm Maya with Redwood, AE on the account. We'll do a quick agenda then go deep on your workload and how reserved pools might look. Liam is our SE. Samir is joining to help with the pilot plan.
[00:18] Dr. Priya Rao: Hi thanks. Quick context, we support clinical summarization pipelines, lots of short-doc inference during business hours and some overnight batch. Main constraint is predictable latency for triage workflows.
[00:33] Carlos Mendes: Yeah and to add, peak qps can double during morning triage 9 to 11 AM, and we also sometimes have spikes when new model releases hit. We're evaluating host vs dedicated, but isolation is a must for PHI.
[00:50] Liam O'Neill: Got it. When you say isolation, do you mean VPC-connect only, or fully private on-prem? Both are supported by Redwood Private or Dedicated with VPC peering depending on the option.
[01:05] Jenna Park: We want VPC peering initially. On-prem is a future conversation but possible. KMS integration is required — keys must be customer-managed. Also audit logs and retention.
[01:20] Maya Chen: Good callouts. On the reserved side we offer dedicated GPU pools you can reserve monthly with burst capacity for short spikes. Burst is a soft layer that lets you go above committed for a short window — we can set thresholds and automatic fallback policies.
[01:35] Dr. Priya Rao: How does fallback work? If reserved pool is full, we failover to hosted instances? We can't risk exposing PHI to shared multi-tenant systems.
[01:45] Samir Patel: Very practical question. We usually implement a routing policy by policy tags — you can tag requests as PHI-only which route to Dedicated pool with enforced VPC. Fallback can be to a private tenant in another region or to a compatible quantized model in your Dedicated fleet — we avoid sending PHI to public hosted endpoints unless you opt-in and sign DPA exceptions.
[02:10] Carlos Mendes: Ok that explains it a bit, but is the burst to other dedicated nodes in the same reservation or to a shared burst pool? What's the SLA behavior — p99 latency guarantees?
[02:25] Liam O'Neill: Burst can be configured two ways: 1) intra-reservation burst (we temporarily overprovision within your dedicated capacity if spare GPUs are available in your cluster) or 2) cross-reservation burst which is best-effort and may not meet strict latency SLOs. Reserved capacity contracts give you more predictable throughput; SLAs are higher for Dedicated reserved pools. For strict p99 targets we recommend a headroom plan in the commit.
[02:50] Jenna Park: We're trying to avoid paying for double capacity but also need latency guarantees. Any tooling to simulate morning spikes?
[03:00] Liam O'Neill: Yes, for pilots we run a benchmark harness — sample load scripts that mirror your real request size distribution and sequence lengths. We also instrument KV cache hit rates and continuous batching behaviour to estimate effective throughput and cost per 1k tokens. I'll share the harness.
[03:20] Theo Alvarez: Procurement question — what are typical reserved contract lengths? Is monthly ok or do we need annual to get burst allowances?
[03:30] Maya Chen: Monthly reserved is available but annual gives better pricing and committed burst credits. For the pilot we usually start with monthly reserved minimums so you can validate.
[03:40] Dr. Priya Rao: We have some legacy models that are large — Llama-70 style family — and we're considering quantized variants. Does Redwood support mixed precision / quantization and does that affect the isolation / fallback story?
[03:55] Samir Patel: We support multiple quantization profiles and model variants. The runtime can pick a quantized variant to reduce memory and increase throughput; we surface model compatibility so fallbacks pick compatible model variants. One caveat: small quantization changes can affect output quality, so we tie those to prompt tests in the rollout.
[04:20] Carlos Mendes: About metrics: we need token-level cost breakdown, per-route dashboards and ability to tag requests per team. How granular is billing with reserved setups?
[04:30] Liam O'Neill: Billing for Reserved is split: baseline commit fee + usage overage (if any). We can expose token-level and model-level telemetry per token/route, and you can instrument cost at request-level with tracing hooks.
[04:45] Jenna Park: Network-wise, what's the peering model? Direct VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink? We have some strict egress rules.
[04:55] Maya Chen: Both are supported; PrivateLink and VPC peering and customer-owned NAT options. We'll share our network diagram. There's also an option for a private control plane for customers needing that.
[05:10] Dr. Priya Rao: Great. Can you speak to patching / kernel selection? Our infra team cares about deterministic execution since we run infer on GPU-GT or similar.
[05:20] Samir Patel: The runtime chooses kernels based on model profile and hardware. We do rolling kernel updates with canarying and automatic rollback. For Dedicated you can request pinned runtime versions for the duration of a release window.
[05:35] Carlos Mendes: If we pin runtime versions, does that impact ability to scale up for burst?
[05:40] Liam O'Neill: It can if pinned versions aren't available on new nodes, but we can orchestrate compatible variants or allow a fallback policy that uses a compatible runtime on burst nodes. We can add that to the rollout playbook.
[05:55] Maya Chen: Quick aside — do you have compliance checklists we should be aware of? Like SOC two, ISO, pen tests?
[06:05] Jenna Park: SOC2 report, KMS/HSM integration, and audit log retention for 365 days are must-haves. We also need data residency in us-east for PHI.
[06:18] Maya Chen: We have SOC 2 type II and can share the report, and KMS integrations are supported for Dedicated and Private. We can also provide per-request audit logs with retention options. I'll include those in the security packet.
[06:35] Theo Alvarez: Timeline wise, we're aiming to sign something by the end of Feb if pilot validates. Any blockers to that besides the pilot?
[06:45] Maya Chen: Contracting cycles and any legal redlines could impact timeline; we'll work with your procurement. Usually pilot -> benchmark -> 30d POC -> expand reserved.
[06:55] Dr. Priya Rao: For the pilot — what constitutes success? We want to validate p95/p99 latency for triage paths, cost per inference at 90% utilization, and no data egress outside our VPC.
[07:08] Liam O'Neill: Perfect. We'll design the pilot to measure p50/p95/p99, end-to-end latency including network hop to your VPC, and cost metrics. We'll also run stress scenarios to test burst and fallback.
[07:25] Carlos Mendes: Can we carve out a short RPS target for the pilot? Eg 200 rps sustained for 20 minutes and 600 rps spike?
[07:33] Liam O'Neill: Yep, that'll be fine — we'll create a ramp script. We typically instrument with 5-10 minute ramps and holding periods.
[07:45] Jenna Park: Regarding data, we need DPA terms for PHI — does Redwood sign BAAs?
[07:50] Maya Chen: We have standard DPA language and can discuss BAAs — that tends to be part of enterprise contracting. I'll flag legal to prep templates.
[07:59] Dr. Priya Rao: On model fallback, we want deterministic failing behaviour rather than silent degrade. Eg, if fallback means different model, we want explicit telemetry and a canary route.
[08:10] Samir Patel: Agreed. We'll add fallback to produce a clear audit event and optionally return a 409-style response or route with a model-version indicator. That will be surfaced in the request trace.
[08:25] Carlos Mendes: Any trials on autoscaling behavior in Dedicated? We don't want cold start latencies for new nodes.
[08:33] Liam O'Neill: Dedicated autoscaling uses pre-warmed images and maintains warm VMs; cold start is minimized. For very tight p99 SLOs we recommend reserved headroom or keep-alive pools.
[08:45] Maya Chen: Let's capture the rough sizing then: you said morning 2x baseline, spikes up to 3x occasionally, mostly short requests, some longer sequences overnight. Jenna, can you share token/sequence distribution?
[08:58] Jenna Park: Sure — I'll export a histogram of sequence length and average tokens, and share by Monday.
[09:05] Maya Chen: Great — that will help us recommend commit size. Based on what I'm hearing, we should propose a baseline reserved pool sized for 150% of average with 2x burst credit for 10-minute windows, plus a pilot harness to validate.
[09:20] Dr. Priya Rao: One more item — encryption at rest with customer KMS, and key rotation policy. We need a model for key rotation without downtime.
[09:30] Samir Patel: KMS rotations are supported; we do staged key rotations with double-write periods to ensure no downtime. We'll share the sequence.
[09:40] Theo Alvarez: For procurement, two asks: 1) we need an itemized price breakdown and commit vs burst pricing, 2) list of standard contract terms and timelines.
[09:52] Maya Chen: Understood. We'll provide that. Any final technical gotchas we should capture?
[09:58] Carlos Mendes: Just to note, we run some heavy beam-search style reranking; we might need pinned lower-latency kernels for that.
[10:08] Liam O'Neill: We'll flag kernel selection and offer pinned runtime for the reranker path.
[10:15] Maya Chen: Cool — let's recap next steps. I'll send pricing and security docs; Liam will send the pilot harness and load scripts; Jenna will share telemetry histograms; Theo will confirm procurement timeline. We'll tentatively schedule a 2-hour pilot kickoff on the week of Jan 26.
[10:33] Dr. Priya Rao: Sounds good.
[10:35] Jenna Park: Thanks everyone.
[10:36] Maya Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the packet.

[End of recording — 58 minutes]

Notes on ASR glitches: 'KV cache' transcribed sometimes as 'K V cash', 'SOC2' sometimes as 'sock two', 'SAML' as 'SMAL' and 'PrivateLink' as 'private link' — please refer to participants for clarifications in follow-up.
